VibePascal v58 -- i386-linux CROSS compiler -- runs on x86_64-linux, emits 32-bit i386-linux
Source commit: dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a
Parent release for THIS target: v54 (b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e)
Built: 2026-09-11 on x86_64-linux, from a CLEAN compiler/i386 unit tree, driven by
       the v58 native ppcx64 (md5 8c8179b2f0a452cebec0131aa301b076)
Binary: bin/ppcross386  md5 b76969a5226f68019f287a97dac89333
                        sha256 0260a27bbc3754749442d70340461c7e1db4e652b6003da1e7b421bf8eb2c9a2
                        6338192 bytes, ELF 64-bit x86-64, statically linked, stripped

THIS TARGET WAS FOUR RELEASES BEHIND.  x86_64 shipped v55, v56, v57 and v58 while
this cross compiler stayed on v54, so it is not a one-fix refresh -- it collects
everything that happened in between:

  v55 (4d10b26fe7)  a missing -FU/-FE output directory is CREATED instead of
                    complained about, so a first build in a fresh directory works.
  v56 (f06e46d8eb)  an inferred inline var initialised from a real constant is a
                    Double, whatever the constant's value happens to be.
  v57 (c31227c8ca)  a half-written .ppu is an ERROR, not an infinite 99%-CPU spin
                    with no message.  On the v54 binary this target was still
                    shipping, a killed build or a full disk could hang a compile
                    forever.
  v58 (dedf242c69)  a .ppu SHORTER than the length its own header declares is
                    rejected instead of silently accepted.  v57 only noticed
                    damage it happened to trip over; lose the TAIL of a unit and
                    there was nothing to trip over, so the compiler built your
                    program against a unit that is not all there -- exit 0, no
                    message.

Nothing in the RTL, the packages or the PPU format changed across v54..v58, so an
existing i386-linux unit set stays valid and does not need rebuilding.

VERIFIED ON THESE EXACT BYTES
-----------------------------
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh ppcross386 i386-linux, against the real
    54220-byte packages/aspell/units/i386-linux/aspelldyn.ppu:
        11/25 offsets clean, 14 problem(s), exit 1   on the v54 binary this replaces
        25/25 offsets clean,  0 problem(s), exit 0   on this one
    Of the 14: 9 truncations HUNG and had to be killed at 30s, and 5 were
    ACCEPTED with rc=0 -- a corrupt unit taken as valid, silently.
    The pre-fix binary is the one that actually shipped as v54, preserved and
    re-run this cycle -- not a reconstruction.
  * EXECUTION, not inspection: this compiler built tests/test/tinlinevarnativeint1.pp
    -Munleashed into an ELF 32-bit i386 binary which RAN on this host and reported
    checks=45 fails=0 NativeInt=4, VERDICT:PASS.

BUILD PROVENANCE, because a cross build can lie about being one
---------------------------------------------------------------
The first attempt this cycle relinked ppcross386 from Sep-3 units: it compiled
ONE file (pp.pas, 795 lines), never touched the patched entfile.pas, and still
emitted a NEW md5 that reads exactly like a successful rebuild.  The unit tree is
now wiped per target before building and the recompiled-unit count is asserted
(277 units for this binary).  If you are reproducing this, check the count, not
the timestamp.

NOT PROVEN HERE: nobody has run this compiler, or anything it emits, on a 32-bit
i386 INSTALL.  The generated binaries were executed on x86_64-linux, which runs
i386 code natively; that covers codegen and RTL, and does not cover a real 32-bit
userland.
